LESSON: WRITING 3.4.1 HANDWRITING

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade two
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.4: Writing 3.4.1 Handwriting
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 3.4.1 Handwriting, part of Strand 3 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade two General.

Key inquiry question: How do we write words?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 3.4.1 Handwriting together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Learning to learn: The learner’s ability to learn independently is enhanced they practice forming ascenders and descenders correctly as an

aspect of good handwriting.

● Communication: The learner’s writing skills are improved as they write clearly and spell words correctly.

Values:
Responsibility: The learner’s ability to care for own and other’s property is enhanced as they take care of digital devices when watching

videos.

Link to Pertinent Contemporary Issues:

Learner Support Programmes: (Peer education and mentorship) The learner interpersonal relationships are enhanced as they assist others

improve their handwriting.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Good handwriting is essential in all learning areas.

27

Suggested Learning Resources:

Video clips, assistive technology such as universal cuffs/wrist braces/arm braces, weighted pencil/pen grips, page-turners, adapted digital devices

Other Related Service Providers: Resource person, speech therapist, Learner support assistance, Occupational Therapist.
